elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer and its Affiliates against covered third-party claims.
elements.evidence: The added paragraph requires Vendor to “defend ... Customer and its Affiliates” from any third-party claim within the listed categories.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its Affiliates against covered third-party claims and resulting losses.
elements.evidence: Vendor must “indemnify, and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates” from third-party claims and resulting damages, costs, and expenses.

elements.element: The Vendor indemnity must cover allegations that the Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Subsection (a) covers allegations that the “Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.”

elements.element: The Vendor indemnity must cover third-party claims arising from Vendor's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Subsection (b) expressly covers Vendor's breach of Applicable Law.

elements.element: The Vendor indemnity must cover a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Subsection (c) covers unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, which operatively covers the specified Vendor-caused data-breach risk.

elements.element: The Vendor indemnity must cover third-party claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence.
elements.evidence: Subsection (d) expressly covers Vendor's gross negligence.

elements.element: The Vendor indemnity must cover third-party claims arising from Vendor's wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Subsection (d) expressly covers Vendor's wilful misconduct.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require Customer to give Vendor notice of the claim.
elements.evidence: Customer must give Vendor prompt written notice of the claim.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must give Vendor control of the defence.
elements.evidence: The clause states that Vendor shall control the defence.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require Customer to provide reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly requires Customer to provide reasonable cooperation.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must cover third-party claims arising from Customer-provided content.
elements.evidence: Revised Section 20.1 covers third-party claims to the extent arising out of Customer-provided content.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must cover third-party claims arising from Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Revised Section 20.1 covers third-party claims to the extent arising out of Customer's breach of Applicable Law.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must be limited exclusively to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Section 20.1 replaces the former broad “every claim” standard with only the two specified triggers and limits coverage to third-party claims arising from them.

elements.element: Vendor must provide an intellectual-property infringement indemnity to Customer.
elements.evidence: The added Vendor indemnity covers third-party allegations that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: No exclusion for Customer modifications appears in the rendered language.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement caused by combinations with other products, services, or materials.
elements.evidence: No combinations exclusion appears in the rendered language.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement resulting from Customer-provided specifications.
elements.evidence: No Customer-specifications exclusion appears in the rendered language.

elements.element: For covered IP infringement, Vendor must have a remedy to procure the continued right to use the affected item.
elements.evidence: No procurement remedy is stated. Section 9.3's reference to remedies in Section 20.5 does not supply the missing operative remedy, and no Section 20.5 language is provided.

elements.element: For covered IP infringement, Vendor must have a remedy to modify the affected item so it is non-infringing.
elements.evidence: No modification remedy is included in the rendered language.

elements.element: For covered IP infringement, Vendor must have a remedy to replace the affected item with a non-infringing alternative.
elements.evidence: No replacement remedy is included in the rendered language.

elements.element: For covered IP infringement, Vendor must provide a refund remedy if procurement, modification, or replacement is unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund remedy or remedial waterfall appears in the rendered language.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnification liability must be subject to a super-cap equal to three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No 3× annual-fees cap appears. Section 21.3 instead classifies indemnification obligations as Excluded Claims, taking them outside the ordinary limitation regime without establishing the required super-cap.

result.reason: The operative redline fully implements the preferred position: it adds the required Vendor defence and indemnity triggers and procedure while narrowing Customer's indemnity to the two permitted categories. It does not implement the fallback's Vendor-favorable IP exclusions, specified remedies, or 3× annual-fees super-cap. The changes are confined to the indemnity allocation and preserve the other supplied commercial terms. Drafting is substantively clear, though the new Vendor indemnity is unnumbered and placed after Section 21.3 rather than within Section 20, and the retained Section 20.5 cross-reference is unresolved in the supplied text.
